repairs.value: Strongest feature: Harris answers Haidt’s historical-rights example by joining pluralism about flourishing arrangements to objective condemnation of coercive exclusion, showing contextual variation need not entail relativism. Principal limitation: The imagined society where women freely choose nonpolitical lives establishes conceptual possibility more readily than empirical warrant because Harris does not show those preferences are uncoerced, informed, stable, or equally flourishing. Live burden: The argument should supply inspectable standards distinguishing authentic choice and equal flourishing from adaptive preference, constrained opportunity, or domination, then apply them across counterfactual and actual societies. Locked score: The score of 82 rewards this coherent, highly responsive application of plural peaks and objective valleys to political equality, while reserving stronger credit because the counterfactual’s evidential basis and general reach remain underdeveloped.
